features.label: ML inference engine tests

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Fixed TextGenerationTest.ProcessDeathDuringGenerateRejects perma failing on tsan

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Run tests using llama.cpp on both processes

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 2: Test the concurrency contracts of TextGenerator

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Run the llama.cpp smoke and perf tests on both paths

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 4: Add host process to ML telemetry

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 2: Route llama.cpp MLEngine to HWInference

patches.author: Joe Bowser
patches.subject: Add a test that the next run waits for a cancelled generation

patches.author: Joe Bowser
patches.subject: Add known-fail tests for runWithGenerator abandonment

patches.author: Tyler Etchart
patches.subject: Added snapshot promises tracking to monitor and updated LLM engine mock to support promise awaits instead of polling to help test flakiness

features.summary: The tests now exercise text generation through both the existing route and the new HWInference process, including llama.cpp smoke and performance checks. They also check that concurrent and cancelled generations are handled in order, and make the tests more reliable by waiting for promises instead of repeatedly polling.

features.label: ML IPC

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 1: Add TextGenerator, WebIDL surface over PTextGeneration

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 3: Add HWInferenceProcess and the browser HWInference process

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 1: Manage PHWInference under PUtilityProcess

features.summary: Firefox now has a WebIDL interface for text generation, backed by inter-process communication (IPC) to an HWInference process hosted by the browser. This gives machine-learning inference a dedicated process to run in, rather than keeping that work in the page or main browser process.

features.label: Native text generation

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 3: Add profiler markers to llama.cpp operations in HWInference

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Implement PTextGeneration with LlamaBackend

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Add PTextGeneration over the browser HWInference process

features.summary: Text generation using llama.cpp is now implemented through the browser’s HWInference process, with IPC carrying requests to the llama.cpp backend. Profiler markers were also added so developers can see how long llama.cpp operations take when investigating performance.

features.label: ML actors

patches.author: Joe Bowser
patches.subject: End the run when a runWithGenerator consumer abandons the generator

patches.author: Joe Bowser
patches.subject: Record engine_run for an abandoned runWithGenerator run

features.summary: A text-generation run now ends if the consumer stops using its generator, rather than continuing work without anyone to receive the result. Firefox also records this abandoned run in its engine telemetry, making this behavior visible in diagnostics.

features.label: ML inference backends

patches.author: Valentin Pollet
patches.subject: Part 1: Make LlamaRuntimeLinker::Init thread-safe

patches.author: Joe Bowser
patches.subject: Report when a cancelled llama.cpp generation has released the backend

features.summary: The llama.cpp runtime linker is now safe to initialize from multiple threads. Firefox also reports when a cancelled text generation has finished releasing the backend, helping ensure later work does not start before the previous run has let go.

features.label: Page extractor tests

patches.author: Florian Quèze
patches.subject: Re-enable tests disabled on macOS 15 AArch64 that pass there on try.

patches.author: Taimur Hasan
patches.subject: Follow redirects within the requested site, and match it by registrable domain

features.summary: Page extraction now follows redirects within the requested site, matching sites by their registrable domain (the shared part such as example.com), and tests that behavior. Tests that had been disabled on some newer Macs were also turned back on after passing there.

features.label: ML engine & pipelines

patches.author: Bryan Johns
patches.subject: Added /answer path for search_the_web

features.summary: The web-search pipeline now includes an `/answer` path, allowing it to provide an answer as part of its search flow. This extends the pipeline beyond simply finding and returning web results.

features.label: Page extractor

patches.author: Taimur Hasan
patches.subject: Report a headless load redirected off-site as a distinguishable block, not a generic timeout

features.summary: Page extraction now distinguishes a page load that redirects away from the requested site from a generic timeout. That makes off-site redirects clearer to identify and handle when Firefox cannot safely continue extracting the page.

features.label: Page extractor docs

patches.author: Taimur Hasan
patches.subject: Add Page Extractor developer documentation

features.summary: New developer documentation explains how to use Firefox’s Page Extractor. It gives developers guidance for working with the feature without needing to piece together its behavior from the code.

features.label: llama.cpp (vendored)

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Declare every about:license notice in moz.build

features.summary: Firefox now explicitly includes every license notice for the vendored llama.cpp library in its about:license page, making the software’s licensing information easier to find and keeping the notices complete.

features.summary: The machine-learning test suite now covers text generation through both inference paths, including concurrency, cancellation, and generator abandonment. It also adds smoke tests for autofill and smart window intent models, and shared end-to-end performance tools that track engine activity and measure runs without tearing down engines before warm-up samples. The suite was also cleaned up to make ONNX backend selection and availability more consistent and to remove unused security-layer plumbing.

features.summary: Firefox added the behind-the-scenes messaging needed for text generation and speech recognition to work with machine-learning models, including checking whether a speech model is available and reporting when a model install is refused or fails. It also introduced a separate hardware-inference process for running supported AI tasks, helping keep that work organized outside the main browser process.

The updates also connect the inference library to the speech-recognition functionality it needs.

features.summary: PageExtractor, Firefox’s tool for collecting information from web pages, can now extract YouTube transcripts by default and avoids waiting twice for a page to be ready. It also records clearer timing and performance data, sends telemetry with client details without using Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP, a privacy-protecting relay), and distinguishes an off-site redirect blocked during a headless load from a generic timeout.

The changes also improve compatibility when a particular Metal math kernel is unavailable, avoid trying to use Metal in a process that cannot support it, and keep the bundled code reproducible when updated; license notices are also declared for about:license.

features.summary: Firefox adds Parakeet, a speech-recognition library that can process speech as it arrives, and drains recognized words as they become available. Recognition results are now grouped and finalized once per spoken utterance, including when the decoder stops producing words, and the model’s memory use appears in about:memory.

features.summary: Firefox’s AI features gained an answer path for web searches, a setting to control how many times the OpenAI engine retries, and more complete per-file details for on-device models in about:addons. Speech recognition is now governed by Firefox’s AI controls, with a Preferences toggle and a permission policy that lets sites’ use of on-device speech recognition be controlled.

Downloads are also attributed to the task that requested them, making it clearer which activity needs the model.

features.summary: A text-generation run now ends if the consumer stops using its generator, rather than continuing work without anyone to receive the result. Firefox also records this abandoned run in its engine telemetry, making this behavior visible in diagnostics.

features.summary: The ONNX inference DOM API, which lets web features run machine-learning models using ONNX Runtime, is updated to ONNX Runtime 1.30. The changes also give remote-process types a structured representation, improving how this information is described within the API.
